subject: Invoice #8472: staging traffic attributed to production - request to hold
messages:
From: Anna Morales <anna@composerlabs.io>
To: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, payments@composerlabs.io
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice #8472 — unexpected usage increase (hold request)

Hi Grace,

We received Invoice #8472 this morning for the period Aug 1–14 and saw a $9,200 overage line that looks unexpected. We've attached a short snapshot from our billing system showing the spike and can also share API logs if helpful (I attached composer-billing-snapshot.pdf).

Our initial check shows a large burst of token usage from a client key that was supposed to be in sandbox/staging. That staging environment should not be billing as production. Can you please:

- Put the invoice on hold while we reconcile?
- Provide a breakdown (by API key and top 10 request timestamps) for Aug 1–14?
- Confirm whether this looks like mis-tagging or duplicate counting on your end.

We'd like to avoid payment disruption, so we're requesting a temporary hold on collection while we sort this out. Please advise next steps and an ETA for the breakdown.

Thanks,
Anna Morales
CFO, Composer Labs
anna@composerlabs.io

Attachment: composer-billing-snapshot.pdf
From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
To: Anna Morales <anna@composerlabs.io>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>, payments@composerlabs.io
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice #8472 — unexpected usage increase (hold request)

Hi Anna — thanks for the note and for the snapshot. I’ve flagged this to billing and our sales ops team (cc’d). We can certainly pause collection while we investigate — I’ll mark this invoice as "under review" in our collections queue immediately.

To help us triage quickly could you confirm the following:
- A representative API key (or the first 8 chars of the key) that you think is staging
- Any requestIDs you can share for the busiest hour(s)

I’ll pull a per-key export for Aug 1–14 and include a top‑10 timestamp list. If the spike is from a sandbox key incorrectly flagged as production on our side, we’ll propose a provisional credit. If it’s a customer-side misconfiguration (staging key used in prod), we’ll document that too and work through next steps for adjustments.

ETA: I’ll have the initial per-key export and top timestamps by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Grace O’Connor
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.inference
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Invoice #8472 — internal triage + provisional credit suggestion

Grace / Kim — looping in billing to grab the raw token export. I ran a quick query in sandbox to surface high-volume keys (attaching the query as a stub). Preliminary look suggests a tenant tag was missing on one of Composer's staging API keys; our routing classified it as production because the tag lookup fell back.

Suggested path:
- Immediately mark invoice 8472 as "on hold" (Grace already did)
- Produce full token_export_20250801-20250814.jsonl and a CSV sample (usage-samples.csv) with top request timestamps and requestIDs
- Offer a provisional credit of up to $1,200 while we complete RCA; if the root cause is on our side (mis-attribution/routing fallthrough) we apply the credit; if it’s a customer key misuse we document and release the hold but discuss next steps.

I’m happy to recommend the provisional credit so we avoid interrupting Composer's operations while we finish the technical review.

Attachment: internal-usage-query.sql
From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
To: Anna Morales <anna@composerlabs.io>, payments@composerlabs.io
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice #8472 — staging traffic attributed to production (investigation results)

Hi Anna — quick update and next steps. Thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary of findings below and attached exports for your review.

Summary:
- Root cause: A Composer staging API key lacked the tenant tag due to a deploy-time config change on Aug 3; our routing logic fell back to the customer's default tenant mapping which treated the key as production. This produced legitimate billed tokens but for the wrong environment.
- Evidence attached: token_export_20250801-20250814.jsonl (per-request detail) and usage-samples.csv (top 50 rows with timestamps and requestIDs). We also uploaded the full export to Drive: https://drive.google.com/fake-link/usage-export-8472

Proposed resolution:
- We will apply a provisional credit of $1,200 to Invoice #8472 while Composer confirms the findings on your side. That credit can be applied to the current invoice or as an automatic offset on your next billing cycle — please tell us the preferred option.
- Collections hold will remain in place until you confirm. If you confirm the staging key should not be billed, we will finalize the credit and close the hold. If you confirm this was production traffic, we will lift the hold and proceed with standard collection.

Next steps for Composer (quick):
1) Confirm you received the attached exports and that the key fingerprint (first 8 chars) matches your staging key (we've redacted full key in attachments).
2) Tell us whether to apply the credit to the current invoice or offset next month.

If you'd like, I can schedule a 30-minute call with engineering to walk through the timestamps — Ben and Kimberly are available tomorrow morning.

Thanks — we’re aiming to make this as seamless as possible.

Best regards,
Grace O’Connor
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.inference
Phone: (415) 555-0193

Attachments: token_export_20250801-20250814.jsonl, usage-samples.csv
